steps.title: Prepare calling pots with virgin females
steps.instruction: Place each virgin female singly into a double‑sided calling pot, seal the pot securely, attach a label that includes the eclosion date, and keep the pots in a cool bag or box for transport to the field site.

substeps.instruction: Insert a single virgin female into a double‑sided calling pot.
Securely seal the pot to prevent escape.
Attach a label with the female’s eclosion date to the pot.
Store the sealed pots in a cool bag/box until travel.

steps.title: Assemble the trap on site
steps.instruction: Insert the dowel into the trap for rigidity; fit the first blue conical vent; attach one or two pre‑assembled female calling pots to the internal velcro strip; fit the second blue conical vent; the trap is now ready for placement.

substeps.instruction: Insert the dowel into the trap frame.
Place the first blue conical vent into the trap.
Attach one or two calling pots to the internal velcro strip.
Place the second blue conical vent into the trap.

steps.title: Position trap >5 m above ground
steps.instruction: Hang the assembled trap more than 5 m above ground using a broken branch, extendable pole, climbing, or portable ladder; rest it against the tree trunk so it does not move in wind; ensure no branches block the entrances; avoid direct sunlight, ant colonies, and small‑bird access; on a hillside place the trap higher up the slope rather than in the valley.

substeps.instruction: Select a site >5 m above ground level.
Secure the trap to a broken branch, pole, ladder, or by climbing.
Rest the trap against the tree trunk to minimise wind movement.
Check that no branches obstruct the vent entrances.
Avoid locations with direct sunlight, ant colonies, or small‑bird access.
On slopes, position the trap higher up the slope.

steps.title: Check trap daily and collect males
steps.instruction: Each morning, inspect the trap; transfer captured males individually into labeled pill boxes or, if many, into a labeled larger cage; perform transfers under a sheet of netting to prevent agitation and escape; keep males together with a record of site and date; avoid exposing males to direct sunlight to prevent wing wear before scoring.

substeps.instruction: Inspect the trap in the morning.
Transfer each male into a pill box with site and trap number label, or place many males into a larger cage with the same labeling.
Conduct transfers under a sheet of netting.
Record the trapping site and date for each batch of males.
Keep males out of direct sunlight to minimise wing wear.

steps.title: Maintain fresh virgin females in trap
steps.instruction: Use females aged day 1–4 after eclosion for optimal attraction; if unavailable, females may be used up to day 7; store unused females at 5–7 °C in a fridge or other cool place; place two females per trap and replace the older female of the pair every two days.

substeps.instruction: Select females that are 1–4 days old post‑eclosion; older females may be used up to day 7.
Store any females not in traps at 5–7 °C.
Place two females in each trap.
Replace the older female of each pair every two days.

steps.title: Record and store captured males
steps.instruction: Euthanise captured males and store them at –20 °C; transfer specimens quickly in small batches to envelopes and back to the –20 °C freezer, minimizing freezer door openings; log each specimen in the Biston_storage_2020_v2.xlsx spreadsheet with site, trap number, and date.

substeps.instruction: Euthanise each male and place it at –20 °C.
Transfer specimens in small batches to envelopes and return them promptly to the –20 °C freezer.
Minimise repeated opening of the freezer.
Enter specimen data (site, trap number, date) into Biston_storage_2020_v2.xlsx.
